page.layout: One page of running text in one column, italic throughout. Running head at top. Page number at top left. Below the text, at the right, a chapter opening "14. De" in large type, placed as a catchword.

p.i: Tu (Domine) potes inflectere utriusque partis corda in utraque Gente, quod fecisti olim hominibus Judah & Israël ut eo David restituerent fidcli[?] ardore, quo illum nuper levitate & impetu fuerant persecuti.
Custodi mihi Amorem Veritatis & Rectitu-dinis, nec desperabo de subditorum affectibus in Me quandoque rediturus.
Tu maria exundantia reciprocari, & retro cogis concedere intra fines à Te praestitutos.
Deus Meus In Te confido, ne erubescam, ne irrideant me Inimici mei, non gaudeant super me, non de me jubilent.
Confundantur omnes iniqua agentes supervacue, revertantur quærentes animam meam.
Integritas & æquitas custodiant me, quia Te exspecto Domine.
Libera Ecclesiam Tuam (Domine) ex omnibus suis angustiis.

page.notes: The Greek running head is transcribed as printed. "fidcli" in the first paragraph is copied as it appears on the scan and is doubtful. "ut eo" reads "ut co" on the scan, and "impctu" may be a misprint of "impetu". Both are copied as seen. The large dots and stains on the page are not printed text and are left out. No marginal notes are visible. The catchword "14. De" is treated as the opening of the next chapter.
